newsitem.title: MEXICO: Two of Mexico's crude ports shut due to winds.
newsitem.headline: Two of Mexico's crude ports shut due to winds.

text.p: Two of Mexico's crude ports remained shut Monday as winds blew at least 40 km/22 miles per hour in the Gulf of Mexico, port authorities said.
Dos Bocas in Tabasco state and Pajaritos in Veracruz state remained shut over the weekend to petroleum exports, officials told Reuters.
Dos Bocas shut Friday at 1405 local/2005 GMT as winds reached 65 km per hour and waves were up to eight feet high.
The Veracruz port was closed on Friday at 1350 local/1950 GMT, and a port captain said the port would probably remain closed until Tuesday.

Cayo Arcas in Campeche state, the nation's largest crude shipping port, reopened 0645 local/1245 GMT Sunday after about a 24-hour closure. A port official said the weather was still adverse and winds clocked at 90 km/55 miles per hour.
According to the latest Pemex figures, Cayo Arcas ships an average 611,000 barrels per day (bpd), Dos Bocas exports about 440,000 bpd and Pajaritos ships about 399,000 bpd
